name: Neutral link, closed
summary: A removable link in the neutral conductor shown in its closed position, allowing the neutral to be opened for testing.
description: A neutral link is a bolted or plug-in link in the neutral conductor, often mounted in a fuse carrier style holder alongside phase fuses. It allows the neutral of a circuit to be disconnected for insulation testing or fault finding without disturbing other circuits on the neutral bar. The closed form shows its normal service state.

The symbol is not a switch and the link should not be opened under load. It does not provide overcurrent protection; the fuse-like holder can mislead readers into treating it as a neutral fuse. Rules on whether the neutral may be separately disconnected differ between earthing schemes.
readingNotes: Do not read the holder as a fuse.
Confirm the link is opened only with the circuit isolated.
drawingChecklist: Label the link with its circuit number.
Show it in its normal closed state.
Check scheme rules for neutral disconnection.
distinction: A closed neutral link is a removable connection; a neutral fuse would be a protective device and is generally not permitted.
